nodes.title: Glossary browser reads and shows a concept's description, marking legacy concepts awaiting one
nodes.summary: use-glossary-concepts.ts now narrows description off the concepts listing, the Concepts tab renders it per concept with a status-dot marker for an empty (legacy) description, and use-concept-options.ts's deliberate omission of description is disclosed as a departure from its sibling's shape.

nodes.title: Named UiErrorState kind for ConceptDescriptionRequiredError
nodes.summary: The central error-ui-state table gains a distinct concept-description-required kind for the backend's ConceptDescriptionRequiredError, carrying no wording, with every existing mapping left untouched.

nodes.title: Concept form authors and validates the description, and its refusal reaches the operator by name
nodes.summary: The existing concept create/edit form gains a required description field through create and edit, submits it in the registration body, and its failure path renders the concept-description-required UiErrorState with its own wording while every other failure still falls through to the generic toast.

nodes.title: Glossary browser description column and legacy marker — proof
nodes.summary: Six new tests across three spec files establish that the concept shape carries description, the Concepts tab renders it, an empty description gets a visible non-invented marker, its column placement, and use-concept-options' continued omission of description.

nodes.title: Proof for the concept-description-required UiErrorState kind
nodes.summary: Two new tests in the existing error-ui-state.spec.ts, in the same per-entry style already used for every prior single-entry addition, prove the new table entry resolves to its own distinct kind and carries no wording; the third criterion is already proven by the untouched pre-existing suite.

nodes.title: Concept form description field — proof
nodes.summary: New tests prove the description field populates on edit, is required, and its own missing-description refusal reaches the operator by name; three sibling spec files from a closed initiative's own delivery are corrected (with the human's explicit authorization) since this task's own required description field legitimately widens the PUT body and the validation surface they exercise.
